minutes.headline: Committee triaged its entire resident feedback list into must-have/nice-to-have priorities, no formal plan votes yet
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee spent most of the meeting working line by line through a spreadsheet of resident-submitted master plan recommendations, sorting each into "must have," "nice to have," or dropping it, covering housing, farmland, small business, community spaces, municipal buildings, schools, and infrastructure. The committee also discussed that the OverUnder consulting contract's completion date has already passed and leaned toward targeting a spring 2026 rather than fall 2025 town meeting presentation, but made no formal decision or vote on the plan's substance.

votes.motion: Motion to approve all previous meeting minutes except last week's, which would be reviewed separately
votes.moved_by: unclear (heard as a member, not the chair)

budget_items.topic: OverUnder master plan consultant contract completion date
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee noted the consultant's contract completion date of January 1, 2025 had already passed with no formal extension confirmed. They planned to establish a new completion date with the consultant's input rather than unilaterally.

budget_items.topic: Contract completion date options tied to town meeting timing
budget_items.what_was_said: Members weighed a completion date tied to presenting at a November special town meeting versus a more realistic date tied to the May annual town meeting.
A member said newly built townhouses in town are priced too high to function as affordable housing.

budget_items.topic: State farm tax credit / minimum acreage for farm status
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed a state law giving a property tax break to parcels over a minimum acreage dedicated to agriculture, and noted the town cannot change this state requirement.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill Elementary renovation vs. new construction cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recounted the school committee's architect estimate that a new building would cost far more than renovating the existing Turkey Hill school.
A member recalled a large sum was spent building a greenhouse into a school building that is now underused, and suggested finding a plan to use it.

budget_items.topic: Monty Tech tuition/assessment paid by the town
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the amount the town pays to send students to Monty Tech is very large relative to how few Lunenburg students actually attend, and floated an in-district trades program as an alternative.

budget_items.topic: OpenGov online payment setup and fees
budget_items.what_was_said: A member warned OpenGov has to be configured carefully, citing being overcharged relative to the correct amount when paying online.

decisions.decision: Agreed to hold meetings on the 2nd Wednesday in person at the rear building and on the 4th Wednesday via Zoom only, due to lack of available meeting rooms.
Agreed to enable Zoom's AI transcription/companion for future meetings to supplement manual minutes.
Emily Young and Sandra Hart were made Facebook page admins for the committee.
Leaned toward setting a more realistic (later) contract completion date for the OverUnder consultant rather than pushing to finish before a fall special town meeting.
Combined several housing feedback items into a single 'encourage diverse housing options' recommendation covering apartments, townhouses, single-family and multifamily housing.
Agreed the town already effectively allows a temporary dwelling on a lot while a home is being built, so struck that as a new recommendation.
Agreed to drop the 'establish an affordable housing trust' recommendation as too legally uncertain.
Combined items into a single recommendation to inventory and create a strategy for protected and unprotected farmland.
Reworded a recommendation to 'encourage bylaws that allow for multi-use agricultural' activity such as agritourism and on-site farm sales.
Marked renovating Turkey Hill Elementary as a must-have, tied to establishing a rolling multi-year school facilities funding plan.
Marked developing an in-district trades training program, as an alternative/supplement to Monty Tech, as a priority.
Marked establishing a dedicated stormwater infrastructure fund as a must-have, noting the town's stormwater task force expects to bring it to a town vote next year.
Marked assessing the feasibility of the town purchasing the town center buildings as a must-have item to investigate.

Agreed to sort the prioritized recommendation list by relevant town committee, circulate it for committee feedback with a target turnaround of about a month and a half, and revisit progress at a future meeting.

what_happened.line: Committee leaned toward a spring 2026 town meeting presentation instead of fall 2025, after noting the consultant's contract completion date had already passed
Marked renovating Turkey Hill Elementary as a must-have, tied to a rolling multi-year school facilities funding plan
Marked a dedicated stormwater infrastructure fund as a must-have, noting the town's stormwater task force expects to bring it to a vote next year
Dropped a proposed affordable housing trust as too legally uncertain
Agreed to sort the prioritized recommendation list by town committee and circulate it for feedback before revisiting progress

why_it_matters: Sliding the master plan presentation to a spring 2026 town meeting means any formal adoption vote residents expected sooner will come later.
Marking Turkey Hill Elementary and a stormwater fund as must-haves signals capital requests that could surface on a future town meeting warrant.
Dropping the affordable housing trust idea narrows which tools the town is considering for affordable housing going forward.
